en: The sampaguita, our national flower, blooms year-round and releases its sweet fragrance mostly at night to attract its specific moth pollinators.
The narra, the national tree, drops its bright yellow flowers in clusters during the dry season before growing its new leaves.
The Ifugao people carved their famous rice terraces into steep mountains, using a complex stone-walled irrigation system to channel natural mountain springs.
The carabao, our national animal, lacks sweat glands and must wallow in mud or water to cool its body temperature.
The perfectly symmetrical Mayon Volcano in Albay is a stratovolcano built up by many layers of hardened lava and volcanic ash.
The Tboli weavers extract strong fibers from the abaca plant stalks to dye and weave their traditional tnalak cloth.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol are made of grass-covered limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season, resembling chocolate.
Hatchling pawikan sea turtles in Morong, Bataan, use the natural moonlight reflecting off the ocean to guide them to the water.
The rare waling-waling orchid grows high on the branches of tall trees in the Mindanao rainforest to access better sunlight.
The Tamaraw, a dwarf buffalo endemic to Mindoro, has distinct V-shaped horns and prefers living in high-altitude grassy clearings.
Fireflies, locally called kiwkik, gather in the leaves of berembang trees along the Loboc River to flash their bioluminescent lights.
The underground rivers in Puerto Princesa flow directly into the sea, creating a unique ecosystem where ocean tides affect the cave.
